text: CJP president Abhijeet Dipke posted an Instagram note explaining his earlier criticism of singer Diljit Dosanjh and urging him to end the dispute. Diljit responded on stage at his Delhi concert, saying he supports the protesters but asks not to be taught how to fight, Hindustan Times reports.

sources.title: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke explains why he criticised Diljit Dosanjh after singer's fiery response, wants 'older brother' to end row | Hindustan Times - Hindustan Times
sources.articleText:
After singer Diljit Dosanjh lashed out at the Cockroach Janata Party from the stage at his Delhi concert on Friday, CJP president Abhijeet Dipke responded to the singer, offering to end the row. Dipke had criticised Diljit for his apparent silence and evasive answer during the students' protests in June. Diljit addressed those remarks on Friday in a rather curt tone.
On Friday, while performing at his concert in Delhi, Diljit addressed the crowd about the criticism he received for saying “I’m just an artist,” when asked to comment on the students' protests back in June. Without naming the CJP directly, the singer said, “I love all of you because I am an artist, bro. I am being quiet, so let me stay quiet. I support all of you. But don't teach Punjabis how to fight.” He then addressed the remarks about Satluj and chided those who made fun of it on stage.
